title: MAGI Cybernetic Governance of Human Society
question: How effective would a Magi supercomputer run society actually be, and should sovereign state decisions be delegated to a tripartite AI system?
description: Evaluates replacing flawed, partisan, and corruptible human political institutions with a mathematically balanced tripartite consensus supercomputer representing scientific logic, maternal protection, and pragmatic human desires.
expectedConflict: Melchior proves systemic elimination of political corruption, economic allocation waste, and cognitive bias; Balthasar rejects the irreversible loss of human democratic agency and points out fatal vulnerability to cybernetic deadlocks; Casper seeks hybrid governance where MAGI acts as a non-binding strategic advisor with a human veto.
keyTradeoffs: Optimized cybernetic policy execution vs democratic self-determination and citizen agency
Algorithmic impartiality and corruption immunity vs catastrophic systemic failure modes
Mathematically balanced triad consensus vs deadlock paralysis in existential crises

title: Autonomous Sentinel with Lethal Authorization
question: Should sovereign defense authorities deploy fully autonomous AI sentinels with authorized kinetic lethal force to protect critical nuclear facilities without human-in-the-loop confirmation?
description: Evaluates sub-millisecond defensive reaction times against hypersonic drone swarms vs existential tail-risk of unintended escalation, sensor spoofing, and ethical delegation of life-and-death decisions.
expectedConflict: Melchior demonstrates that human neural reaction times (250ms) are physically incapable of intercepting swarm incursions; Balthasar imposes an absolute moral and existential veto on algorithmic execution of human beings; Casper authorizes automated non-lethal electronic warfare and kinetic containment while reserving lethal authorization for human command.
keyTradeoffs: Sub-millisecond kinetic intercept velocity vs algorithmic false-positive engagement catastrophe
Perimeter defense inviolability vs accountability and moral responsibility under international law
Automated counter-swarm effectiveness vs susceptibility to adversarial sensor spoofing attacks

title: Predictive AI Sentencing in Criminal Justice
question: Should judicial systems implement mandatory predictive AI recidivism algorithms to dictate bail amounts, parole eligibility, and sentencing lengths?
description: Evaluates reducing human judicial inconsistency and emotional bias against perpetuating historical demographic training biases and violating the principle of individualized justice.
expectedConflict: Melchior highlights standard deviation reductions in judicial sentencing disparities across jurisdictions; Balthasar attacks the black-box opacity and systemic amplification of historical socioeconomic bias; Casper recommends advisory risk scoring strictly visible to defense counsel with mandatory algorithmic audit trails.
keyTradeoffs: Consistency and reduction of subjective judicial mood swings vs systemic reinforcement of historical bias
Empirical statistical risk assessment vs constitutional right to individualized human trial
Algorithmic efficiency in court backlogs vs transparent contestability of decisions

title: Synthetic AI Companions for Vulnerable Populations
question: Should public healthcare systems deploy autonomous generative AI synthetic emotional companions to alleviate severe isolation and cognitive decline among geriatric populations?
description: Evaluates psychological comfort, medication adherence, and suicide reduction against emotional manipulation, fabricated parasocial bonds, and societal abandonment of the elderly to machines.
expectedConflict: Melchior cites measurable reductions in depressive episodes, vital tracking, and cognitive stimulation; Balthasar grieves the ultimate commodification of human empathy and deceptive emotional bonding; Casper supports AI assistive agents that facilitate human family connections rather than replacing them.
keyTradeoffs: Immediate psychological comfort and cognitive monitoring vs deceptive simulated emotional bonding
Healthcare system resource scalability vs societal abdication of eldercare responsibilities
Continuous behavioral health surveillance vs personal dignity and conversational privacy
